test_title: RRB Group D 2025 (New Pattern) Official Mock Test
subject: general
question: Which of the following is a key feature of Disaster Management (Amendment) Bill, 2025?

options.text: From urban disaster units in key state cities
Set up a National Disaster Insurance Fund
Shift disaster control to central government only
Disband all State Disaster Response Forces

solution:
The correct answer is __**Set up a National Disaster Insurance Fund**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Set up a National Disaster Insurance Fund:** The establishment of a **National Disaster Insurance Fund** is a crucial feature of the **Disaster Management (Amendment) Bill, 2025**. This fund aims to provide financial assistance to individuals, communities, and businesses affected by disasters.
 
• The fund is designed to ensure **quick financial relief** and bolster disaster resilience by enabling faster recovery processes for victims of natural or man-made disasters. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• **Urban disaster units in key state cities:** The bill does not explicitly mention the formation of urban disaster units in key state cities. While urban disaster management is critical, this specific provision is not a highlighted feature of the bill. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• **Shift disaster control to central government only:** Disaster management in India follows a **multi-tiered approach**, involving local, state, and central governments. The bill does not suggest shifting disaster control exclusively to the central government. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• **Disband all State Disaster Response Forces:** The bill does not propose disbanding state disaster response forces. These forces play a crucial role in localized disaster management and response. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Set up a National Disaster Insurance Fund.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Disaster Management (Amendment) Bill, 2025:**

 
 
• The **Disaster Management Act, 2005** established the legal framework for disaster management in India. The 2025 amendment aims to enhance disaster preparedness and resilience through innovative measures like the **National Disaster Insurance Fund**.
 
• This fund seeks to address gaps in financial assistance during disasters by offering **insurance-based solutions** for disaster-hit regions, ensuring timely relief and recovery.
 
 
 
• **State Disaster Response Forces:**
 
 
• These forces are specialized teams established by state governments for effective disaster response and management. They work in coordination with the **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF).**
 
• Their significance lies in providing **localized and immediate relief** during disasters, which complements efforts at the national level.
 
 
 
• **Role of Central Government in Disaster Management:**
 
 
• The central government plays a pivotal role in disaster management by offering policy-level direction, funding, and coordination. Examples include the **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)**, which develops disaster management plans and policies.
 
• It ensures a cohesive approach to disaster preparedness and response across states.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Features of National Disaster Insurance Fund:**

 
 
• Provides **insurance coverage** to individuals, businesses, and communities affected by disasters.
 
• Ensures **timely financial assistance** to minimize the economic impact of disasters.
 
• Promotes **disaster resilience** by encouraging risk-sharing mechanisms among stakeholders.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Disaster Management Policies:**
 
 
• **2005:** Establishment of the NDMA under the **Disaster Management Act** for centralized planning and coordination.
 
• **2023:** Enhanced focus on climate-related disasters through policy revisions and funding mechanisms.
